resources.string: Recovery key
On. Your recovery phrase can overrule the server.
Not set up. The server alone controls your identity.
Checking…
Couldn't check. Open to try again.
Your identity is @%1$s, the name people and apps know you by. %2$s hosts your account, and right now it is the only one that can change your identity. A recovery key lets you overrule it.
Your recovery key comes from your 12-word recovery phrase, so there is nothing new to write down. %1$s only receives a public part of the key, which lets it recognize your key but not use it.
Anyone with your 12 words can take control of @%1$s. Store them where only you can get to them.

Turn on recovery key

Turn on your recovery key?

%1$s will add your recovery key to @%2$s and rank it above its own key. From then on, your recovery phrase can overrule changes the server makes to your identity, and the server can't swap your key for a different one.
Turn on

@%1$s has a recovery key made from a different recovery phrase, so this device can't use it. You need the phrase you turned it on with.
To use your recovery key on this device, enter your recovery phrase.

Take back control
If you think someone else changed your identity, or you no longer trust the key %1$s uses for it, replace that key with a new one. Your recovery phrase approves the change on this device.
Replace the server's key

This device approves the change with your recovery phrase. The phrase never leaves this device.
The key %1$s uses for @%2$s stops working, and a new one replaces it.
Your recovery key still ranks above the new key.
Your journal, sign-in methods and devices don't change.
Replace key
